questions.stem: Which of the following anti-asthma drugs is not a reliever?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sodium cromoglycate

Explanation:

  • It is a synthetic hormone derivative which inhibits the degranulation of mast cells (as well as other inflammatory cells) by trigger stimuli. Release of mediators of asthma-like histamine, LTs, PAF, interleukins, is restricted.
  • The basis of this effect is not well understood but may involve a delayed Cl¯ channel in the membrane of these cells inhibiting activation. Long-term treatment decreases the cellular inflammatory response; bronchial hyperreactivity is reduced to variable extents.
  • Bronchospasm induced by allergens, irritants, cold air and exercise may be attenuated. Cromoglycate is not a bronchodilator and does not antagonize the constrictor action of histamine, ACh, LTs, etc. Therefore, it is ineffective if given during an asthmatic attack


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 249

questions.stem: Formoterol is FDA-approved for the treatment of the following conditions except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Aspirin-induced asthma
  • Prophylaxis – inhaled steroids
    Acute attack – Salbutamol

    Explanation:
  • Formoterol is FDA-approved for the treatment of asthma and bronchospasm, prophylaxis of exercise-induced bronchospasm and COPD
  • Long-acting selective β2 agonist which acts for 12 hrs when inhaled. In comparison to salmeterol, it has a faster onset of action. It is used on a regular morning-evening schedule for round-the-clock bronchodilatation. Dose: 12–24 µg by inhalation twice daily
  • Sites of action
  • Primary sites of bronchodilator action of inhaled adrenergic β2 agonists and inhaled anticholinergics. Salbutamol mainly relaxes bronchiolar smooth muscle; Ipratropium blocks bronchoconstriction mainly in the larger airways

questions.stem: Which of the following is a long-acting ?2 adrenoreceptor agonist:
questions.solutionHtml:
Salmeterol
  • It is the first long-acting selective β2 agonist with a slow onset of action which is used by inhalation on a twice-daily schedule for maintenance therapy, as well as for nocturnal asthma, but not for acute symptoms.

  • It is more β2 selective than salbutamol, as well as more lipophilic which probably accounts for its longer duration of action. The concern of asthma worsening due to regular use of inhaled β2 agonists applies to salmeterol as well

questions.stem: Theophylline has antagonist interaction with which of the following receptor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenosine receptors
  • Several mechanisms have been proposed for the actions of methylxanthines, but none have been firmly established. At high concentrations, they can be shown to inhibit several members of the phosphodiesterase (PDE) enzyme family in vitro, thereby increasing concentrations of intracellular cAMP and, in some tissues, cGMP. Cyclic AMP regulates many cellular functions including, but not limited to, stimulation of cardiac function, relaxation of smooth muscle, and reduction in the immune and inflammatory activity of specific cells.
  • MOA

questions.answerText: Thin airway mucus secretions for easier removal by suctioning.
questions.solutionHtml:
Thin airway mucus secretions for easier removal by suctioning.

N-acetylcysteine

  • The mucolytic (mucus-thinning) drug, is given to reduce the viscosity of airway mucus. It has no effects, in the context of pulmonary disease, other than that. It is given by inhalation, usually with a nebulizer in hypertonic saline, mainly to facilitate mucus removal (whether by airway suctioning or by postural changes that allow better drainage from the airways.

questions.stem: Which of the following in its parenteral form is lifesaving in severe status asthmaticus and acts, at least in part, by inhibiting phospholipase A2?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisolone

Prednisolone is a steroid. It is used for the treatment of a wide variety of medical conditions such as severe allergic reactions, asthma, rheumatic disorders and skin and eye disorders. It provides relief by preventing the release of substances that cause inflammation and by suppressing the immune system.

questions.stem: True about Zafirlukast is all except?

options.label: C
options.text: It is effective in acute bronchial asthma

questions.answerText: It is effective in acute bronchial asthma
questions.solutionHtml:
It is effective in acute bronchial asthma
  • Zafirlukast and montelukast are leukotriene receptor antagonists.They cause modest improvement and reduction in asthma symptoms lessening the need for beta-agonist rescue These drugs are considered alternatives to low-dose inhaled corticosteroids in patients with persistent asthma. Zafirlukast is long-acting and can be given once or twice daily orally. It is a modest bronchodilator and reduces asthma morbidity, provides protection against exercise-induced asthma and diminishes nocturnal symptoms.
  • Montelukast is more potent than zafirlukast

questions.stem: A patient comes to you complaining that whenever he takes aspirin for a headache, he develops severe shortness of breath. Which of the following may be partly responsible for this effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leukotrienes
  • Aspirin-induced asthma
    • Aspirin blocks the COX enzyme, production of thromboxane and some prostaglandins is decreased,
    • In patients with aspirin-induced asthma, this results in the overproduction of leukotrienes (LTC-4, LTD-4) from the LOX pathway and produces severe asthma and allergy-like effects.
    • SAMTER’S TRIAD- asthma, ethmoidal polyp, aspirin.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old child has severe asthma and was hospitalized five times between the ages of 7 and 9. He is now receiving outpatient medications that have greatly reduced the frequency of severe attacks. Which of the following is most likely to have adverse effects when used daily over long periods for severe asthma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisone by mouth

Explanation:

  • Systemic use of corticosteroids causes growth retardation. If oral corticosteroids are to be used, alternate-day therapy can be tried. Systemic effects of long-term ICS are clinically relevant only at doses > 600 µg/day. The significant ones are—mood changes, osteoporosis, growth retardation in children, early cataracts, bruising, petechiae, hyperglycaemia and pituitary-adrenal suppression.
  • Several reports of adrenal crises have appeared, especially in children, during stress (of infection, etc).


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 250

questions.stem: After successful treatment of the acute attack, the patient was referred to the outpatient clinic for follow-up treatment of her asthma. Successful strategies currently in use for asthma include all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Blockade of histamine receptors
  • Histamine does not appear to play a significant role in asthma, and antihistaminic drugs, even in high doses, are of little or no value. Rather leukotrienes, PAF, and TNF alpha play a major role
  • The inflammation in bronchial asthma is initiated by mast cells (present in the lungs), and the infiltrate is dominated by eosinophils, lymphocytes and mast cells.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 241

questions.stem: Which of the following is an adverse effect of Minoxidil?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypertrichosis
  • Minoxidil is a very efficacious orally active vasodilator. The effect results from the opening of potassium channels in smooth muscle membranes by minoxidil sulfate, the active metabolite. Increased potassium permeability stabilizes the membrane at its resting potential and makes contraction less likely. Like hydralazine, minoxidil dilates arterioles but not veins.

  • Because of its greater potential antihypertensive effect, minoxidil should replace hydralazine when maximal doses of the latter are not effective or in patients with renal failure and severe hypertension, who do not respond well to hydralazine.


Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology- 15th Edition, chapter 11, Page Number: 13,32

questions.stem: What is the mechanism of action of bosentan?
questions.solutionHtml:
Endothelin Receptor Antagonist
  • Bosentan is the first ERA to be approved for clinical use. Chemically it is a sulfamide and dual ETA-ETB antagonist. Both initial depressor and subsequent pressor response to i.v. ET-1 is blocked.

  • The oral bioavailability of bosentan is ~50%. It is metabolized in the liver by cyp2c9 and cyp3a4, and excreted in bile; plasma t½ is 6 hours. One of the metabolites is active.

  • No dose adjustment is needed in renal disease, but it is contraindicated in liver disease because it causes dose-dependent elevation of hepatic aminotransferases and carries the risk of hepatic injury. Monthly monitoring of liver function tests is mandatory. Other S/E: edema, Anaemia

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: Which of the following is available for SC Injection?
questions.solutionHtml:
Terbutaline
  • Explanation: Only terbutaline is available for subcutaneous injection (0.25 mg). This route is used in case of severe asthma requiring emergency treatment when aerosolized therapy is not available or has been ineffective due to mucous plugging in airways, Inhaled salbutamol and terbutaline are currently the most popular drugs for quick reversal of bronchospasm, but should not be used on a regular schedule. Regular use does not reduce bronchial hyperreactivity: may even worsen it.

  • This may be responsible for the diminished responsiveness that occurs after long-term use of these drugs. Regular use also down-regulates bronchial β2 receptors

questions.stem: The therapeutic range of theophylline is?
questions.solutionHtml:
5-15mg/L
  • The therapeutic range of theophylline is 5-15mg/L
  • It exhibits a narrow therapeutic index
  • Theophylline has a narrow margin of safety. Dose-dependent toxicity starts from the upper part of the therapeutic concentration range.
  • Adverse effects are primarily referable to the g.i.t., CNS and CVS. Headache, nervousness and nausea are early symptoms. Children are more liable to develop CNS toxicity.

questions.stem: More M1 M3 selectivity compared to M2 is shown by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tiotropium bromide
  • Tiotropium bromide is More M1 M3 selectivity compared to M2, tiotropium is less likely to antagonize M2-mediated inhibition of ACh release, which is done by Ipratropium (paradoxical bronchoconstriction)
  • Antimuscarinic agents are effective bronchodilators. Even when administered by aerosol, the bronchodilation achievable with atropine, the prototypic muscarinic antagonist, is limited by absorption into the circulation and across the blood-brain barrier.
  • Greater bronchodilation, with less toxicity from systemic absorption, is achieved with a selective quaternary ammonium derivative of atropine, ipratropium bromide, which can be inhaled in high doses because of its poor absorption into the circulation and poor entry into the central nervous system.
  • Studies with this agent have shown that the degree of involvement of parasympathetic pathways in broncho-motor responses varies among subjects. This variation indicates that other mechanisms in addition to parasympathetic reflex pathways must be involved.


Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology- 15th Edition, chapter 20, Page Number: 10, 28

questions.stem: Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody used for the treatment of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Bronchial asthma
  • It is a humanized monoclonal antibody against IgE. Administered s.c., it neutralizes free IgE in circulation without activating mast cells and other inflammatory cells.
  • On antigen challenge, little IgE is available bound to the mast cell surface receptors (FcεR1) to trigger mediator release and cause bronchoconstriction. In severe extrinsic asthma, omalizumab has been found to reduce exacerbations and steroid requirements.
  • No benefit has been noted in nonallergic asthma. It is very expensive and its use is reserved for resistant asthma patients with positive skin tests or raised IgE levels who require frequent hospitalization. It is being tried in other allergic diseases as well.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 252

questions.stem: The mechanism of action of montelukast is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leukotriene receptor antagonist
  • Montelukast: Since it was realized that cysteinyl leukotrienes (LT-C4/D4) produced by macrophages, eosinophils and other inflammatory cells in the lungs are important mediators of bronchial asthma, efforts were made to develop their antagonists and synthesis inhibitors.
  • Two cysLT1 receptor antagonists’ montelukast and zafirlukast are now established drugs for asthma
  • Both have similar actions and clinical utility. They competitively antagonize cysLT1 receptor-mediated bronchoconstriction, airway mucus secretion, increased vascular permeability and recruitment of eosinophils, used as prophylactic therapy of mild-to-moderate asthma


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 248

questions.answerText: An increase in dose is required in cardiopulmonary disease
questions.solutionHtml:
An increase in dose is required in cardiopulmonary disease
  • Theophylline is well absorbed orally; rectal absorption from suppositories is erratic.
  • It is distributed in all tissues—crosses the placenta and is secreted in milk (V 0.5 l/kg), 50% plasma protein bound and extensively metabolized in the liver by demethylation and oxidation primarily by CYP1A2.

questions.stem: Inhibition of 5-lipoxygenase is useful in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Bronchial asthma
  • Leukotrienes are potent bronchoconstriction agents. These agents play a major role in the pathogenesis of bronchial asthma. The drugs acting by inhibiting their synthesis (i.e. lipoxygenase inhibitors) or action (Cys-LT receptor antagonists) are useful in the prophylaxis of bronchial asthma.

  • Zileuton is a 5-LOX inhibitor, that blocks LTC4/D4 as well as LTB4 synthesis. It therefore has the potential to prevent all LT-induced responses including those exerted by activation of the cysLT1 receptor.

  • However, clinical efficacy in asthma is similar to that of montelukast. The duration of action of zileuton is short and it has hepatotoxic potential. These limitations have restricted its use.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 249
